clue.text: The wind in Jersey?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the gentle west wind, personified in myth as Zephyrus
second meaning: a thin, lightweight sports shirt or jersey

explanation.surface: A question about what the weather is like on the Channel Island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the island, but it is the garment; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Zephyr names the mild west breeze and also a light fine-knit garment worn for sport.

clue.text: Mark rising with tuition here?

indicators.note: in a down entry, something rising is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to mark something is to note it

explanation.surface: A school's marks climbing thanks to good teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a place where pupils receive teaching, so it is somewhere tuition happens.

clue.text: Finding source of beer and whisky in child's play

parts.note: the hop is the plant whose flowers flavour beer
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone discovering a drinks cabinet hidden among children's toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game of hopping through chalked squares, played by children.

clue.text: Yorkshire's a third up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Yorkshire was historically split into three administrative divisions, North, East and West
second meaning: on horseback, as a jockey who is up is mounted

explanation.surface: A claim that a third of Yorkshire is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Old Norse for a third part, which is why there were exactly three of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Each historic division of Yorkshire was called a Riding, and a rider in the saddle is said to be up.

clue.text: Shed's inclination to join the players

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin
a list is a lean, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A garden shed leaning over towards a group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast list is the printed roll of actors in a production, so it stands for the performers.

clue.text: As encountered in 15? The reverse!

parts.note: surface reading: a ghost met in an abandoned town would be the spirit of its old residents
setter's reading: an abandoned town is exactly where the shared neighbourly feeling has gone

explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, a ghost in a deserted town is a spirit of the community; but such a town is the opposite of a place with neighbourly togetherness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a sense of shared belonging among neighbours, which a deserted settlement lacks entirely.

clue.text: He is doomed on stage, but more than one may go about nameless

parts.note: the title figure of a famous Arthur Miller tragedy, a travelling worker who dies at the end

parts.words: more than one may go about nameless
parts.note: the plural of the answer, rearranged, spells the word nameless

explanation.surface: A doomed stage hero, and a crowd of anonymous people wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the plural is an anagram of nameless, which is why the clue says more than one; the singular answer comes from the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Loman, the commercial traveller in Miller's tragedy, is the doomed figure of the stage title.

clue.text: The song Teletubby Tinky-winky's finally taken to heart

indicators.note: taking something to heart puts it in the middle of something else

parts.note: Laa-Laa is the yellow Teletubby of the children's TV show

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the name it follows

parts.note: Tinky Winky is the purple Teletubby; its name ends in this letter

explanation.surface: A child's TV character holding a song close.
explanation.walkthrough: Teletubbies was a BBC pre-school programme; both characters named come from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Layla is the Eric Clapton rock classic recorded with Derek and the Dominos.

clue.text: p evidently preferred to f here!

definitions.text: p evidently preferred to f here!

parts.note: surface reading: a spelling choice of one letter over another
setter's reading: in music p means piano, quiet, and f means forte, loud, so choosing p is choosing the gentle alternative

explanation.walkthrough: Musical score markings: p is quiet, f is loud, so this is literally picking the quiet choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the easy, less demanding choice, here read literally as choosing quietness over loudness.

clue.text: The old men get over abuse that's started us off in the Taj Mahal?

definitions.text: that's started us off in the Taj Mahal?

parts.note: pop and pa are both familiar names for a father

indicators.note: turned over means read the other way round

parts.note: mud is insult, as in mud-slinging

explanation.surface: Elderly fathers recovering from mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taj Mahal is a typical name for an Indian restaurant, where this crisp bread comes as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A poppadum is the thin crisp lentil wafer served before the meal in Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Suspension of work being carried out to hedge

definitions.text: Suspension of work being carried out
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a temporary dismissal of workers
second meaning: a bookmaker passes bets on to others to limit risk

explanation.surface: Building work stopped while a hedge is planted.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedge here is the betting sense, protecting yourself against loss, not a row of bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A layoff is a stoppage of employment, and to lay off a bet is to spread risk with another bookmaker.

clue.text: Commander deployed squadron with it and he gained control

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military leader sends out a squadron and takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish conquistadors were the conquerors who seized power in the Americas.

clue.text: Car phone, apparently hand free

parts.note: automatic, needing no manual operation
a mobile is a cell phone

explanation.surface: A hands-free phone fitted in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay comes after the definition in reverse order: the phone part is read last.
explanation.definitionFit: Automobile is the formal word for a motor car, a passenger road vehicle.

clue.text: It's only fair

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a complaint about fairness; it is two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means merely or simply, and the adjective means morally right and impartial.

clue.text: One sought to contact propagator of mischief, resulting in this

definitions.text: One sought to contact propagator of mischief, resulting in this

parts.note: Roman numeral one
telephoned
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A government reaching out to a troublemaker, and the scandal that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the 1980s affair in which the Reagan administration dealt secretly with Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iran-Contra scandal involved covert US arms sales to Iran, a hostile regime cast as a stirrer of trouble.

clue.text: Source of gold attracting large numbers, originally thriving, now abandoned

definitions.text: Source of gold attracting large numbers, originally thriving, now abandoned

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so its first letter

parts.note: first letter of gold

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

parts.note: a host is a great crowd

indicators.note: originally means at the start of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of thriving
taken as written

explanation.surface: The life story of a gold-rush settlement, booming once and empty now.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue tells the history of a mining camp that boomed and was then deserted by everyone.

clue.text: Be let out of a quiet prison

indicators.note: a garment let out is opened wider, here to make room inside

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
still means silent and calm

explanation.surface: A plea to be released from a silent jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bastille was the Paris fortress prison stormed in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the notorious state jail in Paris whose fall began the French Revolution.

clue.text: With so may executives outstanding, have orders to replace one

definitions.text: With so may executives outstanding, have orders to replace one

parts.note: surface reading: a firm carrying too many unfilled senior posts; may is evidently a misprint for many
setter's reading: an organisation overloaded with bosses at the summit, where heavy is the letters of have put in order with one more

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is hard to pin down exactly; the core sense is a firm with too many managers for its base, and heavy rearranges have plus one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation is called overloaded at the summit when it has too many managers for its workforce.

clue.text: Ring Times about some of the Rev. Charles Dodgson's letters

definitions.text: some of the Rev. Charles Dodgson's letters

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
the multiplication sign
on means concerning

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper reporting on Lewis Carroll's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodgson, alias Lewis Carroll, was an Oxford don; Oxon is the abbreviation put after an Oxford degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduates of Oxford add the abbreviation of Oxoniensis after their degree letters, as Dodgson would.

clue.text: Nothing I serve will hold her

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the run of letters sits within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A tennis player's empty serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Martina Hingis was a Swiss world number one in tennis; serve fits her sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Martina Hingis is a female tennis champion, so she can be referred to as her.

clue.text: Steeplechase observed in 2 or 22

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cross-country horse race for amateur riders
second meaning: the answers to those clues spell compass point, the word to, then another compass point

explanation.walkthrough: The two answers referred to are ETON and STOW: E to N and S to W.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is an amateur jump race over country, and the other answers each run from compass bearing to compass bearing.

clue.text: Uncovered wound, top taken off

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the opening letter, here removed

parts.note: wound as the past of wind: twisted along

explanation.surface: A wound left exposed after its dressing is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound is the past tense of wind, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked means bare or exposed, without any covering.

clue.text: 2''s shuffled pack

indicators.note: shuffling cards mixes them into a new order

parts.note: the numeral two in the plural, as words

explanation.surface: Twos shuffled into a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack things away neatly in storage.

clue.text: Thief changing sides for 5 cents

indicators.note: sides here are right and left, so one is swapped for the other

parts.note: to nick is to steal

explanation.surface: A thief defecting for a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) is replaced by L (left) at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American and Canadian five-cent coin.

clue.text: New bud seen when Thrower gets working round top of garden?

indicators.note: working means being worked over and reshaped

parts.note: Percy Thrower, the famous British TV gardener

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of garden

explanation.surface: A TV gardener tending a plot so new shoots appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Percy Thrower was a much-loved British television gardener of the 1950s to 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Regrowth is fresh growth coming back on a plant, such as a new shoot.

clue.text: Cushion from pressure, etc?

parts.note: a head of steam or water is pressure
etc stands for and the rest

explanation.surface: Seeking a cushion to ease pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrest is a padded support for the back of the head, as in a car seat.

clue.text: Powerful wines getting demolished, the last one from Burgundy

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its parts scattered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last one points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of Burgundy

explanation.surface: Strong wines being knocked back, ending with a Burgundy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinewy means muscular and strong, full of tough tendons.
